blocks.text: Emerging technologies refer to advanced innovations that are transforming how people live, work, and communicate. Technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, and Blockchain are reshaping industries and creating smarter systems for managing data, automation, and connectivity (as shown in Figure 8.1). These technologies drive innovation across healthcare, education, transportation, and agriculture, making processes faster and more efficient. Understanding emerging technologies is vital in today's digital age. They offer new solutions to global and local challenges but also introduce issues such as data security, ethical concerns, and dependence on automation. By learning about these technologies, individuals can better understand their potential, prepare for future developments, and use them to improve society responsibly.

blocks.alt: A central circle labelled smarter systems is joined to four boxes: Artificial Intelligence (learns from data; decides), Internet of Things (devices sense and act), Cloud Computing (storage and computing online) and Blockchain (shared, tamper-proof records). A note says they are used across healthcare, education, transport and agriculture and also raise security and ethical questions.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.1: AI, IoT, Cloud Computing, and Blockchain Working Together to Shape the Modern World. (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.1)
blocks.long_description: The four often combine: IoT devices collect data, the cloud stores it, AI learns from it and blockchain keeps a trusted record.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Emerging technologies like AI, IoT, Cloud Computing, and Blockchain are shaping the next digital revolution, connecting people, data, and devices across the world.
